title: A warehouse plan: expected value and risk
intro:
Illustrative data, made up for this book. A logistics firm's plan to automate a warehouse has these possible net gains over three years ($ thousand) with their probabilities:

| Gain ($k) | −600 | −150 | 300 | 800 | 1500 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Probability | 0.05 | 0.20 | 0.40 | 0.25 | 0.10 |

Give the expected gain and the standard deviation (the risk), each to one decimal, and the probability of losing money, P(gain ≤ 0), to two decimals.

In the Workbench: **Discrete distribution**, **Distribution** *Typed table of (x, P(x))*, type the values and probabilities, and set **Value of interest (k)** to 0.

StandardDeviation.says: That is the variance, in ($k)². The risk is its square root, in $k.

hints: Var(X) = Σ (x − E[X])²·p(x); the standard deviation is its square root.
P(gain ≤ 0) adds the probabilities of the losses.
